title: Action figures: the category
description: Poseable figures representing characters, typically 3.75 to 12 inches tall, form one of the largest toy categories in the world.

title: G.I. Joe (1964)
description: Hasbro launched G.I. Joe in 1964 as a 12-inch poseable figure, coining the term action figure.

title: Star Wars figures (1978)
description: Kenner's 3.75-inch Star Wars line set the scale standard that dominated action figures for decades.

title: Transformers (1984)
description: The Hasbro and Takara line of converting robots made transformation itself the play algorithm.

title: LEGO minifigures (1978)
description: The LEGO minifigure arrived in 1978 and has since been produced by the billions.

title: Play patterns across the category
description: Narrative algorithms dominate action-figure play: figures act out evolving stories.

title: Backdrop pairings
description: Fantasy-world and space backdrops suit adventure figures and their missions.

title: Safety and standards
description: ASTM F963 governs toy safety in the United States, including action figures.
